label: text
text: Owing to a state of extreme emergency suddenly arising, machine guns had to be used against rioters at Hankow yesterday.

label: text
text:
Hankow, June 11.
Following false reports in this morning's vernacular papers, an anti-foreign riot took place this evening.

label: text
text: The volunteers were called out. The rioters rushed the Bund. They tore up seats and wrought destruction in Japanese shops. They severely mauled a Japanese shopkeeper.

label: text
text: Later the rioters broke down a barricade and attempted to rush the British volunteer armoury.

label: text
text:
The rioters were in heavy numbers totally outnumbering the defence force of the armoury.
The fire brigade ineffectually turned hoses on the mob after which, there being a state of extreme emergency, under orders of the Navy, the rioters were fired on with machine guns.

label: text
text: Eight were killed. The number of wounded is not yet known. At present all is quiet and the Chinese authorities guaranteed continued peace.

label: text
text: [Hankow, June 11.—Following a coolies' dispute last night at Messrs. Butterfield and Swire's upper wharf, in which a great deal of stone throwing took place, a squad of Chinese police fired over the crowd and scattered it. A dozen arrests were made. The trouble was apparently purely Chinese, but this morning when the upper wharf coolies attempted to resume work they were mobbed and prevented from doing so.

label: text
text: A strike was declared, the students haranguing the coolies.—Reuter.]

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: The Note takes cognisance of the fact that the Powers view the incident in the same conciliatory spirit as the Chinese Government and that instructions have been given to the police of the International Settlement to cease the use of arms.

label: text
text: The Note goes on to insist that the steps taken by the authorities of the Settlement to hinder a "pacific student demonstration" were badly devised and denies that there was the state of imminent danger to which the Powers' communication referred.

label: text
text: The Concession authorities and not the unarmed students are therefore responsible for the deplorable events. The Government, in view of the indignation prevailing to-day throughout the country, begs to give general advice to the Concession authorities which the latter should follow, namely to raise the state of siege, re-embark the marines, disarm the volunteers and police, free the arrested men, restore the occupied schools, for the restoration of order in Shanghai with the briefest possible delay.

label: text
text: The Note asks the Ministers to instruct their consular representatives accordingly.

label: text

It was a sad blow yesterday when the employees of the Aquarius mineral water factory joined the ranks of the hood-winked strikers. Still, at a pinch one can mix it with plain water instead, or even ignore any addition, as they do in the country of origin, so the wound is not fatal. Messrs. Caldbeck, Macgregor and Company have been in existence for sixty and something odd years—one forgets in the general excitement whether it is one year more or one year less than the life of the "North China Daily News"—and this is the first strike the Company has ever experienced, which is a good illustration of the depth of absurdity to which the working classes have fallen under the influence of Bolsheviks.
The Hongkow market showed signs of life yesterday morning and quite a few Chinese gardeners brought their vegetables to sell. The Russian and Japanese stall keepers have been doing business all the time. There was no meat to be had here however.

label: text
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text: A mass meeting of 25,000 students and workers was held at the recreation ground in the Shanghai Chinese city yesterday evening under the auspices of the Citizens Association. The participants wearing black arm bands made stirring speeches.

label: text
text: Resolutions were passed (1) to sever economic relations with the British and Japanese on June 12; (2) to urge the Central Government to secure satisfaction for the shooting on May 30 from the British and Japanese; and (3) failing settlement in a fortnight to declare at general strike throughout the country.

label: text
text: The meeting afterwards marched in procession to the native city. During the march two Japanese posing as Chinese students were violently handled and taken to a police station and locked up.

label: text
text: Special trains: conveyed the crowds to and from the native city and the Chapel suburb.

label: text
text: Two Chinese at work on the s.s. Hyson lying at anchor in the harbour were in the act of discharging yoga into a sampan controlling two of their confederates on Wednesday night when a parrot launch appeared on the scene. All four men jumped into the water, but not all managed to get away at one fell into the hands of the Police. About 200 fathoms of the ship's rope valued at $1,000 had been sent over the side. The arrested man was charged at the Kowloon Magistracy this morning and sentenced to one month's hard labour.

label: text
text: Mr. McNeill added that for some time past the British Government had been giving close attention to the question whether industrial conditions were playing an appreciable part in the general widespread unrest in China.

label: text
text: Mr. McNeill expressed the opinion that such conditions were hardly operative at all as the cause of the present troubles, though any such discontent as far as it existed should be welcomed as the symptom of a desire for better things.

label: text
text: He pointed out that the strike began in a Japanese cotton mill where the conditions were equal or superior to anything in China.

label: text
text: Mr. McNeill declared that the British Government had long been exerting active pressure on the international authorities at Shanghai to secure improved factory conditions in the foreign settlement, especially as regards child labour with the aim of making the settlement a model for the rest of China. It now intends to seek a solution of the difficulties in a conciliatory spirit while insisting on the maintenance of law and order in the foreign settlement.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: Finally Mr. McNeill stated that a warning had been given before the police fired, but he was without official information of the precise nature of the warning. He also did not know the number of students arrested and subsequently released but had requested a report on these matters.

text: Hotel Staffs Back.

label: text
text: Mr. Walter J. Hawker, manager of the Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels Ltd., yesterday received a telegram from Mr. J.H. Taggart, who is in Shanghai, to the effect that the situation there is easier.

label: text
text: The Majestic, Palace and Kalee Hotels staffs have already resumed work; and the Astor House Hotel staff is resuming work.

label: text
text: Mr. Taggart proposes to leave for Hongkong on Monday next.

Pakkai, Kongmoon, June 10.
Labourers have ceased work and students have struck. A demonstration took place in the streets of Kongmoon to-day to express sympathy with the strikers in Shanghai.
